risk_of_bias.note: Provisional, like the card's rating. I would rate critically low confidence. (1) Item 11 should be 'no'. AMSTAR 2 asks for a justification for combining the data, and the card itself says pooling cumulative proportions over follow-up of 1 to 20 years with I² of 96% to 99% is not justified in the text; no prediction intervals are given either. With item 7 counted as a flaw, as the card's recorded rating already does, that makes two critical flaws. If the supplement turns out to list the excluded studies, item 11 alone still gives low. (2) The card's item 4 note says a strict reading ('no') would not change the recorded overall. It would: with item 7 as recorded it also makes two critical flaws. Gray literature is excluded without a reason; the English-language limit does have one (resources and expertise, Limitations, 6th paragraph). So partial yes on item 4 holds only on the lenient reading of publication restrictions, the same open question as for Hall 2026.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor, with one addition: the abstract misstates two of the pooled figures (alcohol 10% and sedatives 9%, where Table 2 has alcohol 9% and sedatives 10%), and the Discussion puts both 'below 10%'.

missed: The abstract swaps the alcohol and sedative figures (abstract: alcohol 10%, sedatives 9%; Table 2: alcohol 9% (6–15), sedatives 10% (7–15)), and Discussion, 1st paragraph, puts both 'below 10%'.

Search Results, 1st paragraph: 6097 − 5906 − 141 = 50 full texts were eligible before the 4 hand-searched papers were added, which would give 54, not the 50 stated (editors' arithmetic; the PRISMA figure is an image).

Denominators (editors' calculation from Tables 1 and 3): the 'Other' diagnostic-system subgroup in Table 3 has 2 studies and 459 subjects. In Table 1 those are the Thai cohort (1116 people, 40% followed up) and Wright (1988, 10). So the Thai cohort entered with about 449 people, its followed-up share (40.2% of 1116), not 1116. The S&E Asia subgroup (954) fits the same reading (449 + 80% of Chen's 606 + Singal's 19 = 953). The pooled proportions therefore appear to be shares of those followed up, although the Methods define the outcome as a proportion of the original cohort. This also bears on the card's operationalization field, which leaves the denominator open.

Pooled Rate, 1st paragraph: brief and atypical (26 estimates) plus NOS (18) make 44, against 34 for that group in Table 2; and the 'between-group Q 5,830, df 3' equals Table 2's overall Q. Minor and not about substances.

Comparison field (unmeasured_premorbid): the places cited do not mention family history. Clinical and Service Implications, 4th paragraph, names younger age, longer untreated psychosis and impaired premorbid social function as likely predictors. Limitations, 5th paragraph, lists duration of psychosis, symptom scores, global functioning and ongoing use as too rarely reported.
